label: Cartographic Field
skill_body:
# Playable Visual Essay

Turn the subject into a visual world whose objects, geometry, and changes carry the argument. Do not
imitate The Pudding branding, proprietary fonts, exact artwork, project assets, or distinctive
compositions. Apply only the assigned profile and invent an original subject-specific expression.

## Make the model the composition

Choose one dominant world, object, field, path, or mechanism. Let labels, evidence, and controls attach
directly to it instead of surrounding it with dashboard chrome. Keep object identities and spatial logic
stable when the page changes state.

- Prefer direct annotation, meaningful crop, scale changes, and persistent geometry.
- Use HTML for copy and controls, SVG for exact semantic geometry, and Canvas only for dense or
  performance-sensitive fields.
  a visual world, hero model, state sequence, data field, annotated model, or statement with evidence.
- Treat the assigned profile as the page's material and motion vocabulary, not as a template to copy.

## Invite meaningful action

Add interaction only when the reader's action can become evidence, understanding, or narrative state.
classification, allocation, construction, navigation, path choice, optimization, or trace drawing.

When useful, keep a page-local in-memory reader trace and reflect an observed action or derived result
back into a later state on the same page. Ground every personalized statement in captured events; never
infer personality, emotion, diagnosis, identity, or another sensitive trait. Do not require localStorage,
server persistence, or another page to complete the experience.

## Compose motion and copy

Use semantic motion such as trace, isolate, stack, scatter, flood, replay, zoom, crop, or return. Motion
must reveal an information change, not decorate the page. Keep controls visually subordinate to the
world and label them with short domain actions. Prefer one headline, direct labels, and compact evidence
over explanatory prose.

Reject generic card grids, detached KPI panels, decorative icons, fake game controls, sliders that do
not affect the model, and animation without information change.

## Assigned direction: Cartographic Field

Use for geography, distribution, movement, place, spatial memory, or many observations across a territory.

## Visual DNA

- map/field is the canvas, not a chart inside a panel
- data marks become visual texture at scale
- local labels appear only where story demands
- zoom level is a narrative device

## Composition

- map coverage 65–100%
- copy can float in clear regions of the field
- legends should be embedded/direct where possible
- geographic shapes may bleed beyond slide edges

## Never

- tiny choropleth inside a card with a giant legend
- pan/zoom purely for spectacle

## Scale and spacing recipe (1280x720)

- Display/hero type 64-104px; page title 40-56px; section heading 24-32px.
- Body copy 17-21px with 1.5-1.65 line height; captions and annotations 13-15px.
- Outer margins 48-72px. Major gaps 24-40px; related items 12-16px.
- Treat these as the working range for this canvas, not as acceptance rules.
  Depart from them when the composition earns it.

## Component grammar

- Build structure from the assigned composition's spatial logic, not from a
  generic header/content/footer stack.
- One dominant carrier per page. Supporting elements attach to it rather than
  forming a second competing region.
- Borders, dividers, and shadows are structural. Use `--notale-line` for
  separation and reserve accents for meaning.

## Page contract

- Emit exactly one root element carrying `data-notale-page`.
- Use the injected `--notale-*` tokens. Never redefine them, never invent new
  token names, and never approximate a token with a literal hex value.
- Headings use `--notale-font-display`, body copy `--notale-font-body`, code
  `--notale-font-mono`.
- Everything is offline: no CDN, no remote fonts, images, scripts, or fetches.
- Interaction must run a real algorithm, never a scripted fake.
- The `text_role` counts in the assigned composition are hard caps. Fix overflow
  by cutting content, never by shrinking type or spacing.

compositions.name: World Model
compositions.use_when: The subject is a place, network, or field whose geometry carries the argument.
compositions.spatial_logic: One continuous coordinate space fills the canvas. Labels attach directly to positions in it; nothing is relocated into a legend.
compositions.text_role: One orienting line of at most 16 words plus 2-6 attached labels of 6 words.
compositions.variation: Change the crop and zoom between pages while keeping object identities and orientation stable.
compositions.avoid: A separate legend box, floating cards over the map, resetting the coordinate frame between pages.

compositions.name: Hero Mechanism
compositions.use_when: One object or mechanism must be understood before anything built on it.
compositions.spatial_logic: The object sits large and near-centre with real breathing room. Detail is revealed in layers over the same silhouette rather than in separate panels.
compositions.text_role: One naming line of 4-10 words plus at most five callouts of 8 words.
compositions.variation: Vary which layer is foregrounded and the viewing angle; keep proportions constant.
compositions.avoid: Exploded views by default, the object shrunk to make room for prose, callout boxes with borders.

compositions.name: State Sequence
compositions.use_when: The same system must be read at several moments and the change between them is the point.
compositions.spatial_logic: Repeated instances of one persistent object across an ordered axis. Position and identity stay fixed so only the changing property moves.
compositions.text_role: Three to five states, each labelled in at most 6 words, plus one summary line of 18 words.
compositions.variation: Vary the number of states and whether the axis is time or magnitude.
compositions.avoid: Redrawing the object differently per state, unequal spacing without meaning, arrows substituting for visible change.

compositions.name: Data Field
compositions.use_when: A distribution or population is the evidence and individual cases still matter.
compositions.spatial_logic: Every record is a mark in one shared field. Encoding is stated once at the edge and never repeated per mark.
compositions.text_role: One reading line of at most 18 words plus at most four annotations of 8 words.
compositions.variation: Vary the encoding channel and whether outliers are named; keep the field shape stable.
compositions.avoid: Chart junk, a legend that repeats the axis, aggregating away the individual marks.

compositions.name: Annotated Workbench
compositions.use_when: The reader runs or tunes something and the result must be read against its source.
compositions.spatial_logic: A working surface paired with the artifact that drives it, sharing one alignment. Output appears next to its cause, not in a console far away.
compositions.text_role: One instruction of at most 14 words plus at most six inline annotations of 5 words.
compositions.variation: Vary the ratio of source to result and whether output is inline or adjacent.
compositions.avoid: A detached console strip, controls scattered around all edges, hiding the driving artifact.

compositions.name: Essay Statement
compositions.use_when: The essay pauses to assert, ask, or turn before the next movement.
compositions.spatial_logic: Type dominates over a quiet ground, with one fragment of the visual world bleeding in at an edge to keep continuity.
compositions.text_role: One statement of 8-20 words plus at most one attribution or prompt of 12 words.
compositions.variation: Vary which edge the world fragment enters from and how much of it shows.
compositions.avoid: A blank slide with a centred sentence, quote marks as ornament, losing the visual world entirely.
